question: An unconscious accident victim is rushed in. What legal concept allows you to give emergency care without their verbal consent?

options.A: Expressed consent
options.B: Mandatory consent
options.C: Informed consent
options.D: Implied consent

explanation: You got it! When a patient can't speak and their life is in danger, the law assumes ('implies') they would want you to save their life.

question: What is the main underlying cause of Type 1 diabetes mellitus?

options.A: Gradual resistance of muscle cells to insulin
options.B: Severe dietary deficiency of essential vitamins
options.C: Autoimmune destruction of pancreatic beta cells
options.D: Temporary hormonal changes during pregnancy

explanation: In Type 1 diabetes, the body's immune system mistakenly attacks and destroys the insulin-making beta cells in the pancreas. Keep up the great study habit!

question: How do targeted drugs like rituximab help fight lymphoma cells?

options.A: By blocking all blood vessels feeding the tumor
options.B: By attaching to cell markers and flagging them for immune destruction
options.C: By replacing damaged DNA strands inside the cell
options.D: By telling the liver to make extra clotting factors

explanation: Targeted therapy acts like a smart missile. It sticks to a specific tag on the cancer cell so your immune system can spot and destroy it easily.

question: How is a research hypothesis different from a research question?

options.A: A hypothesis is always written in the form of a question
options.B: A research question contains independent variables only
options.C: A hypothesis is a declarative statement of predicted outcome
options.D: A research question can never be tested statistically

explanation: Questions ask what might happen, but hypotheses make a bold, clear statement of what you predict the results will be.

question: What was the main goal of classical management theory in the workplace?

options.A: Emotional counseling for all employees
options.B: Efficiency and standardized tasks
options.C: Flexible work hours and remote shifts
options.D: Democratic voting on all organizational policies

explanation: Classical management was all about maximum speed, clear chains of command, and doing tasks the exact same way every time like a machine.

question: Why might a doctor prescribe a topical NSAID gel instead of pills for sore joints?

options.A: It provides localized relief with fewer systemic side effects
options.B: It permanently restores lost joint cartilage
options.C: It cures the disease much faster than pills
options.D: It completely eliminates the need for physical therapy

question: About how long is the adult female urethra?

options.A: 20 cm
options.B: 12 cm
options.C: 4 cm
options.D: 45 cm

explanation: Spot on! The female urethra is quite short, measuring about 4 centimeters long.

question: Which drug is commonly used first when a mother has postpartum hemorrhage from a soft uterus?

options.A: Insulin
options.B: Paracetamol
options.C: Oxytocin
options.D: Furosemide

question: What is the primary focus of qualitative data analysis in healthcare research?

options.A: Measuring the exact blood pressure drop after medication
options.B: Counting how many hospital beds are filled each night
options.C: Calculating exact drug dosages and patient body weights
options.D: Exploring human experiences, feelings, and recurring themes

question: Which of these patients is NOT at risk for Wernicke encephalopathy?

options.A: A patient recovering from weight loss surgery who vomits a lot
options.B: A patient eating a balanced diet with normal digestion
options.C: A patient on long-term kidney dialysis without supplements
options.D: A patient with an eating disorder who refuses to eat

explanation: You nailed it! Someone with normal nutrition and digestion gets plenty of daily thiamine, so they are not at risk.

question: In research, what does the 'validity' of a questionnaire mean?

options.A: Whether the tool can be completed in under ten minutes
options.B: Whether the tool measures what it is intended to measure
options.C: Whether the tool was printed on approved institutional paper
options.D: Whether the tool gives the exact same scores on repeat testing

explanation: Validity checks if your questions are truly capturing the specific concept or variable you set out to study. You're building solid clinical research skills!

question: What is a major benefit of providing clear and transparent information to quarantined individuals?

options.A: It shortens the biological incubation period
options.B: It cures underlying viral infections
options.C: It improves cooperation and reduces anxiety
options.D: It replaces the need for daily temperature checks

explanation: Clear communication helps people understand the process, which calms fears and encourages them to stick to the rules. [learn more](GST114_U2_T16#GST114_U2_T16_h6)

question: How does an overly competitive and hostile classroom climate affect students?

options.A: It speeds up the mastery of human anatomy
options.B: It breeds stress and fear of asking questions
options.C: It removes all forms of academic anxiety
options.D: It encourages open sharing of clinical techniques

explanation: Hostile environments make students terrified of looking foolish, which stops them from asking the vital questions they need to learn.

question: Which government program became the main payer for long-term nursing home care after 1965?

options.A: Medicare
options.B: The Hill-Burton fund
options.C: Social Security
options.D: Medicaid

explanation: Medicaid was built to support low-income individuals, and over time it grew to become the primary financial backbone paying for long-term stays in nursing facilities.

question: When is the best time to talk about end-of-life wishes and care planning with the family?

options.A: As early in the disease trajectory as possible
options.B: When the patient develops sudden aspiration pneumonia
options.C: Immediately after the final post-mortem examination
options.D: Only after the patient becomes completely mute and bedbound

explanation: Having these conversations early lets the patient share what they want while they still can, making future medical choices much easier for everyone involved.

question: What is the primary focus of the DASH diet for managing high blood pressure?

options.A: Eating plenty of fruits, vegetables, and low-fat dairy while reducing sodium
options.B: Eliminating all carbohydrates completely from daily meals
options.C: Eating only raw meat and root vegetables
options.D: Drinking large amounts of herbal teas and liquid supplements

explanation: The DASH diet emphasizes nutrient-dense whole foods and mineral-rich produce while cutting back on salt and unhealthy fats. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T16#GNS324_U4_T16_h4)

question: How long should a standard temperature compress usually stay on the skin?

options.A: 15 to 20 minutes
options.B: 1 to 2 hours straight
options.C: Exactly 60 seconds
options.D: Until the patient falls asleep overnight

explanation: Keep it to 15 to 20 minutes. This gives the therapeutic effect without risking skin breakdown or unwanted side effects.

question: Why are the bones of the fetal skull separated by sutures and fontanelles during childbirth?

options.A: To prevent the cerebrospinal fluid from building up inside the cranial cavity
options.B: To allow the skull bones to overlap and change shape inside the pelvis
options.C: To protect the baby's brain from normal changes in maternal blood pressure
options.D: To provide extra room for rapid brain growth during the first stage of labour

explanation: The gaps in the skull allow the bones to shift and overlap, reducing the head's diameter so it can pass safely through the birth canal. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T14#GNS121_U6_T14_h1)

question: You are an unscrubbed nurse walking past a sterile table. What is the safest way to move around it?

options.A: Keep your back turned so you don't breathe on it
options.B: Face the sterile table while walking past it
options.C: Walk close behind the scrub nurse's back
options.D: Reach across the table quickly to save time

explanation: Always keep your eyes on the sterile field and maintain a safe distance so you don't accidentally brush against it.

question: A patient with active pulmonary tuberculosis is admitted to the ward. Which intervention is most crucial to interrupt the airborne transmission of this disease?

options.A: Providing the patient with disposable plastic utensils
options.B: Placing the patient in a negative pressure isolation room
options.C: Washing all hospital floors with ordinary tap water daily
options.D: Encouraging family members to wear clean cloth gloves

explanation: Airborne pathogens require specialized ventilation, such as negative pressure rooms, to prevent them from spreading through the air to other areas. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T95#GNS214_U1_T95_h3)

question: A nurse manager creates a strict handwashing policy to prevent infections, relying on standard operating procedures. Which theory is primarily applied here?

options.A: Bureaucratic management theory
options.B: Human relations management theory
options.C: Pure contingency management
options.D: Quantitative management science

explanation: Establishing formal rules, standard operating procedures, and safety regulations reflects bureaucratic theory. [learn more](GST321_U1_T3#GST321_U1_T3_h6)

question: What is the main drawback of using a 24-hour dietary recall to check a patient's nutrition?

options.A: It can only be performed on hospitalized surgical patients
options.B: It requires expensive laboratory equipment to analyze
options.C: It measures body fat percentage instead of food intake
options.D: It relies heavily on the patient's memory and honesty

explanation: Patients can easily forget what they ate or misjudge portion sizes, which can make your dietary data a bit off.

question: What do we call inflammation of the middle layer of the eye, which includes the iris?

options.A: Keratitis
options.B: Conjunctivitis
options.C: Retinitis
options.D: Uveitis

explanation: You got it! Uveitis is inflammation of the uvea (the middle layer). It can cause a deep, aching pain and make the eyes very sensitive to light.

question: What is an ectopic pregnancy?

options.A: A multiple pregnancy where twins share the same amniotic sac
options.B: A condition where the placenta separates too early from the uterine wall
options.C: A pregnancy that develops normally inside the upper part of the uterus
options.D: A pregnancy where the fertilized egg implants outside the uterine cavity

explanation: Ectopic means out of place, so an ectopic pregnancy occurs when implantation happens outside the main uterine cavity, most often in a fallopian tube. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T29#GNS216_U5_T29_h1)

question: How has modern surgery for primary bone tumors changed over the years?

options.A: Amputations are performed immediately without trying chemotherapy first
options.B: Radiation is now the sole treatment used for all bone cancers
options.C: Limb-salvage procedures have largely replaced routine amputations
options.D: Surgeries are now completely avoided in favor of long-term antibiotics

explanation: Thanks to awesome tech and medical advances, doctors can often remove just the diseased bone and reconstruct the limb instead of doing an amputation.

question: What is the primary public health goal of nurse-led immunization services in primary clinics?

options.A: To provide routine nutritional supplements to infants and toddlers
options.B: To build community-wide herd immunity against preventable diseases
options.C: To completely eliminate all known chronic medical conditions
options.D: To cure active bacterial infections in hospitalized patients

explanation: Immunizations are specifically designed to protect populations by creating immunity against infectious, vaccine-preventable diseases. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T73#GNS214_U1_T73_h1)

question: What do we mean by 'molecular mimicry' in autoimmune conditions?

options.A: A pathogen shares protein structures with body tissue, confusing the immune system
options.B: Antibodies completely change their shape to match a virus
options.C: Immune cells hide inside healthy organs to escape detection
options.D: Healthy cells pretend to be foreign invaders to trick white blood cells

explanation: Sometimes a germ looks very similar to our own body tissue. When the immune system fights the germ, it accidentally attacks the body tissue too because they look like twins!

question: At what time of day is a blood test most accurate for checking testosterone levels?

options.A: Right before bedtime
options.B: Late afternoon
options.C: Immediately after a heavy meal
options.D: Early morning

explanation: Testosterone levels naturally peak in the early morning hours, so doctors prefer drawing blood then for the most reliable results.

question: Why is pushing an endotracheal tube 'blindly' dangerous in severe upper airway trauma?

options.A: It causes sudden high blood pressure.
options.B: It can worsen a tear and completely block the airway.
options.C: It stops intravenous fluids from working.
options.D: It permanently paralyzes the vocal cords.

explanation: Exactly right! Forcing a tube past swollen and damaged tissues can easily push through an existing tear, completely losing the airway.

question: A patient shares that her husband constantly insults her, threatens to chase her out, and cuts her off from her family. What kind of abuse is this?

options.A: Traditional coercion
options.B: Psychological abuse
options.C: Physical maltreatment
options.D: Economic violence

explanation: Well done! Constant insults, threats, and isolation are designed to crush a person's self-esteem and mental peace.

question: What structure marks the point where nerve fibers exit the eye to form the optic nerve?

options.A: Optic disc
options.B: Pupil
options.C: Retina
options.D: Macula

explanation: The optic disc is the anatomical convergence point where nerve fibers leave the eye and appears as a yellowish-pink structure during the exam. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T8#GNS221_U2_T8_h2)

question: Which of these is NOT a normal sign of post-abortion recovery?

options.A: Mild intermittent cramping similar to menstrual periods
options.B: Severe lower abdominal pain that worsens over time
options.C: Light spotting that gradually decreases over days
options.D: Occasional mild fatigue following the procedure

explanation: Pain that keeps getting worse instead of better is a warning sign that something needs medical attention. Great job spotting the abnormal finding!

question: If a patient's satellite cells are completely used up over time due to a chronic condition, what is the most likely result?

options.A: Immediate conversion of skeletal muscle into cardiac muscle
options.B: Inability of the muscle to properly repair itself after injury
options.C: Permanent loss of the blood supply to the affected limb
options.D: Rapid increase in the total number of new muscle fibers

explanation: Without satellite cells, muscles lose their natural healing power, leading to poor recovery and scarring. Understanding this helps us care better for our patients!

question: How does placenta percreta differ from a simple placenta accreta?

options.A: Accreta occurs in the first trimester, while percreta occurs only at term.
options.B: Accreta involves the urinary bladder, while percreta stays inside the uterine cavity.
options.C: Percreta affects only the fetal membranes, while accreta affects the umbilical cord.
options.D: Percreta penetrates through the entire uterine wall, while accreta attaches only to the surface of the muscle.

explanation: Think of 'percreta' as breaking completely *through* the wall of the uterus, sometimes even touching nearby organs like the bladder. It's the most severe form! [learn more](GNS121_U6_T6#GNS121_U6_T6_h4)

question: A ward manager notices missed medication doses and sloppy handovers. What is the most likely underlying issue?

options.A: Low staff morale and diminished workplace motivation
options.B: An unexpected surplus of advanced diagnostic medical equipment
options.C: Excessively high patient satisfaction survey scores
options.D: Too many mandatory training workshops on patient empathy

explanation: When morale dips low, even simple daily routines like handovers can start slipping. Recognizing this helps us support one another better.

question: Which type of measuring tape should a nurse avoid using when checking body circumferences?

options.A: Fiberglass tape marked in centimeters
options.B: Steel tape with a rigid housing case
options.C: Non-stretchable synthetic measuring tape
options.D: Cloth tape that can stretch over time

explanation: Correct! Cloth tapes stretch out with repeated use, which will give you wrong numbers. Always go for non-stretchable tapes for accurate results.

question: What serious brain complication can happen if a patient's blood pressure shoots up dangerously high from nephritis?

options.A: Hypertensive encephalopathy
options.B: Bacterial meningitis
options.C: Cerebellar atrophy
options.D: Peripheral neuropathy

question: Why is an ectopic pregnancy considered a medical emergency?

options.A: It automatically causes permanent infertility in every affected woman

options.C: The developing fetus will grow too large for the mother's abdomen
options.D: It always results in severe high blood pressure for the mother

question: What is the absolute first thing you must do when an adverse event happens?

options.A: Ensuring immediate patient safety and stabilization
options.B: Calling a lawyer to discuss legal liability
options.C: Writing down every detail in the official logbook
options.D: Notifying the hospital director immediately

explanation: Patient care always comes first! Before any paperwork or reports, we must make sure our patient is safe and stable.

question: What is the main goal of Essential Obstetric Care (EOC)?

options.A: Reducing the overall cost of hospital-based maternity services
options.B: Ensuring every birth occurs in a tertiary specialist hospital
options.C: Providing routine antenatal health education to community groups
options.D: Preventing and managing life-threatening maternal and neonatal complications

explanation: Essential Obstetric Care is all about those life-saving interventions that keep both mother and baby safe during pregnancy, birth, and after delivery. You've got this!

question: What physical sign involves a bluish color of the skin due to low oxygen in the blood?

options.A: Jaundice
options.B: Pallor

options.D: Erythema

question: A patient is diagnosed with glaucoma caused by blocked fluid drainage in the front of the eye. What fluid is building up?

options.A: Blood plasma

question: Which of these is a key frontline duty for a community health nurse in disease control?

options.A: Identifying and reporting unusual illness clusters to authorities
options.B: Manufacturing vaccines in centralized laboratories
options.C: Managing international travel restrictions at airports
options.D: Writing national health laws in the legislative assembly

explanation: You've got this! As a nurse in the community, you are often the first to notice unusual sickness patterns and sound the alarm.

question: What term is used for pale, bulky, and foul-smelling stools caused by unabsorbed fats?

options.A: Melena
options.B: Steatorrhea
options.C: Hematochezia
options.D: Glycosuria

question: In which specific part of the fallopian tube does fertilization normally occur?

options.D: Fimbriae

question: Where do nursing research ideas usually begin?

options.A: A personal financial grant from the hospital board
options.B: An unanswered question or gap in nursing knowledge
options.C: The personal opinion of the chief medical director
options.D: A mandatory command from the ministry of health

question: You are nursing a patient undergoing chemotherapy who has a dangerously low white blood cell count. What is your top priority action?

options.A: Practicing strict hand hygiene and enforcing protective isolation measures
options.B: Encouraging the patient to eat fresh, unwashed raw fruits and salads daily
options.C: Avoiding all vital sign checks to prevent disturbing the resting patient
options.D: Allowing large groups of visitors to visit at any time to boost morale

question: What is the primary clinical difference between acute pain and chronic pain?

options.A: Acute pain only affects internal organs, while chronic pain is restricted to skin and muscles
options.B: Chronic pain responds immediately to simple opioids, whereas acute pain requires complex nerve blocks
options.C: Acute pain serves as a sudden warning sign of tissue injury, while chronic pain persists long after healing
options.D: Acute pain causes severe anxiety, while chronic pain never has any psychological impact

explanation: Acute pain acts as a protective alarm for recent injury, whereas chronic pain lasts past normal healing time and becomes a long-term condition. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T14#GNS321_U4_T14_h2)

question: Why is coordination so important when a hospital divides work into many specialised tasks?

options.A: To eliminate the need for any written nursing care plans
options.B: To ensure all nurses perform the exact same medical procedure
options.C: To reduce the total number of working hours per shift
options.D: To prevent fragmented care and bring individual efforts together

explanation: Exactly! When different specialists handle different pieces of patient care, coordination ties everything together so nothing falls through the cracks.

question: Which two theatre team members are primarily responsible for performing surgical counts?

options.A: Radiologic technologist and orderly
options.B: Surgeon and lead anesthesiologist
options.C: Patient and attending physician
options.D: Scrub nurse and circulating nurse

explanation: The scrub nurse and circulating nurse team up to carefully count and record all instruments, sponges, and needles used.

question: A patient is scheduled for an MRI. What is the most critical safety check for you to do first?

options.A: Ensuring the patient drinks two liters of water
options.B: Testing the patient's blood pressure and pulse rate
options.C: Checking if the patient has eaten any food that morning
options.D: Screening for implanted metal devices or pacemakers

question: What crucial step must a researcher complete with participants before collecting any data?

options.A: Medical insurance details
options.B: Employment contracts
options.C: Informed consent
options.D: Financial donations

explanation: Patients must always agree willingly to join your study after you explain what will happen. Getting informed consent is a non-negotiable ethical rule!

question: What is the main job of a medication like loperamide?

options.A: Coating the stomach lining to prevent acid reflux
options.B: Stimulating water absorption by increasing salt intake
options.C: Killing all parasites living in the large intestine
options.D: Slowing down intestinal motility to reduce stool frequency

question: What is a common immediate complication right after FGM is performed?

options.A: Rheumatoid joint inflammation

options.C: Early onset menopause
options.D: Severe hemorrhage and shock

question: What is the main purpose of nursing counseling during a woman's first pregnancy confirmation visit?

options.A: To build trust, provide essential health education, and address emotional reactions
options.B: To perform surgical procedures that permanently confirm the gestational age
options.C: To prescribe powerful medications that completely eliminate morning sickness
options.D: To diagnose underlying psychiatric disorders before the first trimester ends

explanation: Nursing is about care and connection! Early counseling helps moms process their feelings, learn good nutrition, and feel safe in your care.

question: What would happen to the accessory sex glands if a man's testosterone levels dropped very low?

options.A: They would shrink and decrease their secretions
options.B: They would grow larger and produce excess fluid
options.C: They would immediately start producing female hormones
options.D: They would convert into urinary storage tissues

question: What does 'cultural negotiation' mean when caring for patients at home?

options.A: Trading hospital supplies for traditional ceremonial artifacts

options.C: Blending harmless traditional remedies with modern medical care
options.D: Letting the client manage their disease entirely without medicine

question: What is the main way we define gender-based violence (GBV)?

options.A: Harmful acts based on sex or gender identity
options.B: Violent crimes committed exclusively against adult males
options.C: Accidental domestic injuries occurring at home
options.D: Physical injuries sustained during a street fight

explanation: GBV happens because of a person's sex or gender roles, rather than just random bad luck or street crime. You've got this!

question: Why do public health campaigns often focus mass deworming programs on school-aged children?

options.A: Children have the highest worm burdens and engage in behaviors that spread eggs
options.B: Adults are completely immune to reinfection after adolescence
options.C: Deworming tablets are only approved by regulators for pediatric use
options.D: Children are the only population that can develop lung complications

explanation: Kids play outside in the soil and tend to carry the highest number of worms, making school deworming programs super effective.

question: What are the three core components of the epidemiological triangle used in public health?

options.A: Source, vehicle, and victim
options.B: Agent, host, and environment
options.C: Bacteria, virus, and fungus
options.D: Reservoir, vector, and portal

explanation: Great job! Think of it as a three-way relationship: the Agent (the germ), the Host (the person), and the Environment (the surroundings).

question: Why is a 'just culture'—where nurses can report mistakes without fear of punishment—so important?

options.A: It removes all legal liability from the hospital organization
options.B: It encourages honest reporting of mistakes so systemic flaws can be fixed
options.C: It ensures that negligent staff members never face disciplinary action
options.D: It eliminates the need for incident report documentation

explanation: A just culture focuses on fixing broken systems rather than just blaming individuals. When people aren't terrified to speak up, everyone learns and patients stay safer!

question: Which of these is the main feature of a benign tumor?

options.A: It travels through the blood to distant organs
options.B: It has poorly differentiated cells
options.C: It remains localized and does not spread
options.D: It invades surrounding nearby tissues

explanation: You got it! Benign tumors stay put in one place. They don't invade nearby tissues or spread around the body like malignant ones do.

question: What are the three core elements that make a study a true experimental design?

options.A: Manipulation, control, and randomization
options.B: Sampling, blinding, and qualitative coding
options.C: Observation, interview, and transcription
options.D: Surveying, coding, and theme generation

question: When should you release the pulled skin tissue when doing a Z-track injection?

options.A: Immediately before pushing the plunger down
options.B: Before cleansing the skin site with an alcohol swab
options.C: After the needle has been completely withdrawn
options.D: While the needle is still inside the muscle tissue

question: What is the main route of transmission for the pathogens that cause gastroenteritis?

options.A: Fecal-oral route
options.B: Broken skin contact
options.C: Direct droplet inhalation
options.D: Vector-borne mosquito bites

explanation: Gastroenteritis pathogens spread primarily when microscopic amounts of infected stool contaminate food, water, or hands and enter a new host's mouth. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T20#GNS313_U2_T20_h2)

question: Why do symptoms only show up a year after a person first gets infected?

options.A: The adult worm takes that long to migrate and approach the skin

options.C: The larvae remain dormant in the stomach for twelve months
options.D: The parasite only produces toxins after it leaves the human body

question: A mother feels defensive when asked about her child's diet. What approach should the nurse use?

options.A: Use open-ended, non-judgmental questions to explore current practices
options.B: Hand her a detailed textbook and ask her to read it alone
options.C: Report the mother immediately to the hospital social worker
options.D: Scold the mother so she takes the nutritional advice more seriously

question: What common struggle among family caregivers should you always watch out for during follow-up visits?

options.A: Excessive financial wealth
options.B: Overconfidence in surgical skills
options.C: Desire to change careers
options.D: Burnout and depression

explanation: Looking after someone with a long-term brain condition is heavy work, both physically and emotionally. Always check in on how the caregivers are holding up!

question: Which of these actions is a serious example of research misconduct?

options.A: Giving participants the right to withdraw

options.D: Making up survey results to match what you want to prove

question: In public health, what does the term 'herd immunity' mean?

options.A: The body builds resistance to infections through natural dietary intake
options.B: High vaccination rates in a community protect vulnerable unvaccinated people
options.C: White blood cells group together to surround and isolate a foreign microbe
options.D: Animals transmit specific infectious diseases directly to human populations

question: Which of these snacks is safest to give a toddler just as it is, without cutting it first?

options.D: Whole raw baby carrots

explanation: Well done! Soft bananas mash up easily and don't pose the hard, sticky, or round risks that nuts, carrots, or candies do.

question: What is one of the main goals of a nurse acting as a patient advocate in reproductive health?

options.A: Prosecuting doctors who violate hospital budgets
options.B: Writing new national criminal codes in parliament
options.C: Protecting patient rights and pushing for fair access to safe care
options.D: Setting insurance premiums for fertility clinics

explanation: As an advocate, you stand up for your patients' rights, fight against unfair treatment, and help them access the care they deserve. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T8#GNS216_U1_T8_h9)

question: Which everyday habit causes a person to swallow extra air?

options.A: Sleeping on the left side
options.B: Chewing gum
options.C: Eating green leafy vegetables
options.D: Drinking plain water slowly

explanation: Chewing gum makes you swallow air without realizing it, which adds to the gas buildup in your tummy. Good to know for patient teaching!

question: A nurse is caring for four emergency patients. Which patient should the nurse attend to FIRST?

options.A: A patient with a minor scalp laceration needing stitches
options.B: A patient with a closed wrist fracture in mild pain
options.C: A patient with severe stridor and throat swelling
options.D: A patient complaining of a mild headache for three days

explanation: Stridor indicates an upper airway obstruction, which is an immediate life threat that takes top priority over pain or minor injuries. [learn more](GNS315_U2_T2#GNS315_U2_T2_h8)

question: Why does community health nursing place a strong emphasis on health maintenance?

options.A: It completely eliminates all infectious diseases from a population
options.B: It shifts the nurse's job entirely to administrative desk work
options.C: It makes physical examinations completely unnecessary for adults
options.D: It reduces the need for expensive hospital care by stopping illness early

explanation: Focusing on wellness helps catch problems early and keeps people out of hospital beds. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T2#GNS225_U2_T2_h1)

question: Where does intrapersonal conflict take place?

options.A: Between a nurse and a patient
options.B: Entirely inside an individual person
options.C: Across the entire hospital board
options.D: Between two different nursing units

explanation: Intrapersonal conflict is an internal psychological struggle happening strictly within one person's mind and heart. [learn more](GST321_U5_T3#GST321_U5_T3_h2)

question: Why should nurses understand how different healthcare sectors work?

options.A: It gives them the authority to open private pharmacies
options.B: It allows them to manage the hospital budget directly
options.C: It exempts them from clinical documentation duties
options.D: It helps them navigate patient referrals and financial barriers

explanation: As a nurse, you'll often guide patients through complex health systems. Knowing your way around different sectors makes discharge planning and referrals much smoother.

question: When do you check the Apgar score for a newborn baby?

options.A: At birth and every ten minutes
options.B: At one and five minutes after birth
options.C: At thirty minutes and one hour
options.D: At five and fifteen minutes after birth

explanation: You got this! We check the Apgar score right at 1 minute and 5 minutes of life. This helps us see how well the baby is adjusting to breathing on their own outside the womb.

question: What is the normal resting heart rate range for a healthy adult?

options.A: 60 to 100 beats per minute
options.B: 80 to 140 beats per minute
options.C: 40 to 60 beats per minute
options.D: 100 to 120 beats per minute

explanation: You've got this! A healthy adult's heart normally beats between 60 and 100 times per minute while resting. This keeps enough blood flowing to all parts of the body.

question: What is the difference between data fabrication and data falsification?

options.A: Fabrication applies to nursing, falsification applies to physics
options.B: Fabrication is inventing fake data, while falsification is altering real data
options.C: Fabrication is legal with IRB approval, falsification is never allowed
options.D: Fabrication is stealing text, falsification is stealing money

explanation: You got it! Fabrication means making numbers up from thin air, while falsification means tampering with real results.

question: What does the 'halo effect' mean during a performance appraisal?

options.A: Focusing only on mistakes made during the last week of the year
options.B: Rating every single staff member as average to keep the peace
options.C: Allowing one positive trait to result in an entirely high evaluation
options.D: Giving a nurse a poor review because of a single past argument

explanation: The halo effect happens when a nurse is so charming or great at one specific thing that the manager accidentally gives them top marks everywhere else, even where they need work.

question: A patient with a new tracheostomy needs airway suctioning. Why is this considered skilled care?

options.A: It is a basic personal hygiene task that any family member can perform.
options.B: It replaces the need for daily medication administration.
options.C: It is only performed once a year during an annual physical exam.
options.D: It requires specialized clinical knowledge to prevent airway occlusion and infection.

explanation: Keeping an airway clear takes specialized training and sharp monitoring to stop dangerous complications like breathing trouble. Excellent work!

question: A stroke patient is too weak to hold a spoon or brush their teeth. According to Virginia Henderson, what should you, the nurse, do?

options.A: To prescribe nutritional supplements for faster recovery
options.B: To discharge the patient immediately to family members
options.C: To assist the patient with activities they cannot currently do alone
options.D: To wait until the patient regains full strength without helping

explanation: Spot on! Henderson taught us that the nurse's role is to step in and act as hands or strength for the patient when they can't quite manage on their own yet.

question: Why does our body reabsorb most digestive fluids further down the intestines?

options.A: To stop bacteria from growing in the large intestine
options.B: To prevent severe dehydration from fluid loss
options.C: To recycle digestive enzymes for chewing food
options.D: To keep the stool completely liquid at all times

explanation: Our body pours liters of fluid into the gut every day! Reclaiming that water lower down is super important so we don't dry out.

question: Which action directly targets a human reservoir to stop an infection from spreading?

options.A: Boiling all municipal drinking water before distribution
options.B: Placing metal wire mesh over livestock feed storage
options.C: Spraying heavy insecticides around outdoor garbage dumps
options.D: Administering curative drug therapy to clear the pathogen

explanation: Giving medications clears the germs right out of the human body, turning off that human reservoir.

question: How is cancer-related fatigue different from everyday tiredness?

options.A: It does not improve with regular rest or sleep
options.B: It exclusively affects older adult populations
options.C: It only occurs during the first week of diagnosis
options.D: It can only be treated with high-dose intravenous vitamins

explanation: Cancer fatigue is heavy and overwhelming. Unlike normal tiredness, sleeping or resting doesn't make it go away.

question: What is the main drawback of a positive Mantoux (tuberculin skin) test?

options.A: It cannot distinguish between latent and active infection
options.B: It only works in patients who have never received vaccinations
options.C: It is completely unreliable for diagnosing immunocompromised adults
options.D: It requires laboratory analysis of blood within two hours

explanation: A positive skin test simply means your immune system has seen TB before. It cannot tell if the infection is sleeping (latent) or active.

question: Where do endocrine glands release their hormones directly?

options.A: Extracellular tissue spaces
options.B: The lymphatic vessels only
options.C: Ducts leading to the skin
options.D: The bloodstream

explanation: Think of endocrine glands as ductless delivery systems. They pour their chemical messengers straight into the blood so they can travel all over the body!

question: Why must you, as the nurse, use great care when collecting laboratory specimens?

options.A: It decreases the overall cost of running hospital diagnostic equipment
options.B: It ensures the lab results reflect the true condition of the patient
options.C: It shortens the length of time the patient stays in the hospital
options.D: It removes the need for doctors to physically examine the patient

explanation: Spot-on! Good collection habits prevent errors and contamination, meaning the doctor gets accurate results to treat your patient properly.

question: What is the main purpose of evaluating a health promotion program?

options.A: To increase the cost of purchasing imported drugs
options.B: To check if the program achieved its goals and used resources effectively
options.C: To prove that the government needs no further assistance
options.D: To find reasons to dismiss junior healthcare staff

explanation: Evaluation helps determine what worked well, what failed, and how future health interventions can be improved. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T3#GNS225_U2_T3_h9)

question: Which imaging test is the absolute go-to choice for getting a clear picture of brain and spinal tumors?

options.A: Magnetic Resonance Imaging
options.B: Bone densitometry scan
options.C: Standard chest X-ray
options.D: Abdominal ultrasound

explanation: Spot on! MRI gives doctors the sharpest, most detailed look at soft tissues like the brain and spinal cord, making it the favorite tool for spotting nervous system growths.

question: How can experiencing a severe illness during childhood affect a person later in life?

options.A: It ensures the individual becomes a proficient medical doctor
options.B: It completely eliminates any fear of normal aging processes
options.C: It can create a lasting hypersensitivity to bodily vulnerabilities
options.D: It guarantees immunity against developing anxiety disorders

explanation: Early life bumps and health scares can teach a child that the human body is super fragile, planting the seeds for health anxiety down the road.

question: Why should you regularly check the status indicator light on an AED machine?

options.A: To calibrate the internal thermometer for accurate skin readings
options.B: To measure how many shocks are left in the main computer processor
options.C: To ensure the voice volume is loud enough for a noisy room
options.D: To confirm that the internal battery and system components are operational

explanation: Routine checks make sure the machine is ready to work the exact second an emergency happens. Good nursing practice!

question: A newborn has rigid, tightly locked overlapping skull bones after a very long, difficult labour. What do we call this?

options.A: Physiological moulding
options.B: Benign moulding
options.C: Transient moulding
options.D: Pathological moulding

explanation: Well done. When the bones are jammed together tightly from a difficult, prolonged labour, it's considered pathological moulding and needs close attention.

question: Why is the Trait theory considered a bit limited in modern nursing?

options.A: It requires every nurse to have advanced surgical training
options.B: It focuses too much on patient vital signs instead of administration
options.C: It ignores how leadership skills can be learned and shaped by situations
options.D: It proves that nurses never make good ward managers

explanation: While personal traits matter, Trait theory forgets that anyone can learn leadership skills and adapt to different situations on the ward.

question: What major problem prompted the creation of the essential drugs concept?

options.A: Hospitals had too many doctors and not enough clinical space
options.B: Pharmaceutical companies refused to sell medicines to developing nations
options.C: Countries wasted money on redundant drugs while lacking basic treatments
options.D: Patients refused to take any form of modern pharmaceutical care

explanation: Early global health planners noticed limited budgets were being squandered on ineffective remedies instead of life-saving basics. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T2#GNS215_U1_T2_h2)

question: Which blood-borne pathogen carries the highest risk of infection after just a single accidental needle-stick injury?

options.A: Hepatitis C virus
options.B: Hepatitis B virus
options.C: Human immunodeficiency virus
options.D: Cytomegalovirus

explanation: Hepatitis B has a very high concentration in the blood, making it the most easily transmitted pathogen following a needle-stick accident.

question: A clinic treats every patient with the same high standard of care, whether they are rich, poor, or from any tribe. What quality dimension is this?

options.A: Timeliness
options.B: Effectiveness
options.C: Efficiency
options.D: Equity

explanation: Spot on! Equity means fairness. No patient's background or pocket should ever determine the quality of care they receive from you. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T2#GNS312_U5_T2_h2)

question: What big problem can happen with combined city sewer systems during heavy rainstorms?

options.A: Electrical pumps inside homes automatically reverse their flow
options.B: The municipal water pressure drops to zero across the entire city
options.C: Overflows can dump raw, untreated sewage directly into natural water bodies
options.D: Underground pipes freeze solid because of rapid temperature drops

explanation: When storm water and sewage share the same pipes, heavy rains can easily overwhelm the system. When this happens, raw, untreated waste spills straight into local rivers or lakes.

question: Why must instrument cleaning and brushing be done submerged under water?

options.A: To make the detergent foam up much faster
options.B: To prevent infectious droplets from splashing into the air
options.C: To cool down the metal before it gets handled
options.D: To save clean water from running out too quickly

explanation: Scrubbing in the open air creates fine mists that staff can inhale or that can contaminate surrounding sterile surfaces. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T68#GNS214_U1_T68_h1)

question: What is an example of community mobilization in primary health care?

options.A: Organizing residents to clear stagnant gutters and clean their surroundings
options.B: Admitting severe emergency cases into private wards
options.C: Ordering medical equipment directly from international manufacturers
options.D: Writing academic research papers for international journals

explanation: Community mobilization brings local people together to take collective action on health issues like environmental sanitation. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T7#GNS124_U2_T7_h6)

question: As a nurse, what is our main goal when trying to stop a secondary injury after head trauma?

options.A: To permanently numb the patient to eliminate all pain
options.B: To reverse the torn nerve fibers caused by the initial crash
options.C: To prevent further cell death by maintaining oxygen and blood flow
options.D: To repair fractured skull bones without surgery

explanation: Well done! Since we can't always undo the initial impact, our nursing care focuses heavily on keeping oxygen and blood flowing so swelling doesn't destroy more brain cells.

question: What is the clinical benefit of providing a wide variety of choices in family planning services?

options.A: The clinic can avoid stocking pills and focus only on injectables
options.B: It eliminates all possible side effects associated with hormones
options.C: Clients can choose contraception that fits their personal lifestyle and health needs
options.D: Nurses can force every client to use long-acting contraceptives

explanation: Brilliant! Giving clients options respects their autonomy and helps them find a method that genuinely matches their lifestyle and health profile.

question: How must strong opioid medications be kept safe on a nursing ward?

options.A: Inside a double-locked secure metal cabinet
options.B: Unsecured in the main treatment preparation room
options.C: Inside the patient's bedside bedside drawer
options.D: On an open shelf near the nurse's main desk

explanation: Controlled substances like opioids are always kept under double locks to prevent theft and ensure they only go to the patients who truly need them.

question: In the SMART framework for setting goals, what does the letter 'M' stand for?

options.A: Meaningful
options.B: Measurable
options.C: Mandatory
options.D: Managed

explanation: 'M' is for Measurable! It means we include numbers or clear indicators so we can track our progress and see how well we are doing.

question: Which medication group is commonly given to treat roundworms by paralyzing them so the body can pass them out?

options.A: Non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs
options.B: Inhaled corticosteroid anti-inflammatories
options.C: Broad-spectrum beta-lactam antibiotics
options.D: Benzimidazoles like albendazole

question: Which life process helps the body sense changes around it and react?

options.A: Differentiation
options.B: Excretion
options.C: Reproduction
options.D: Responsiveness

explanation: Responsiveness is your body's alert system! It's how you detect things like heat, cold, or pain and react quickly to stay safe. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T1#GNS111_U1_T1_h3)

question: What is the most important advice for a patient who just received IV contrast dye?

options.A: Stay strictly in bed for the next two days
options.B: Take a strong antibiotic pill
options.C: Avoid eating any protein for the rest of the day
options.D: Drink plenty of fluids to help flush the dye out

question: Which of these terms describes multicellular parasitic worms?

options.A: Bacteria
options.B: Helminths
options.C: Ectoparasites
options.D: Protozoa

explanation: Spot on! Helminths are multicellular worms (like tapeworms and roundworms). Protozoa are tiny and single-celled, while ectoparasites hang out on the outside of the skin.

question: Which patient group is often extra sensitive to standard drug doses because their organs are still developing or slowing down?

options.A: Middle-aged office workers
options.B: Young adult athletes
options.C: Healthy school-age children
options.D: Infants and elderly adults

explanation: Both the very young and the elderly process drugs differently because their livers and kidneys are either not fully grown yet or starting to slow down.

question: What is a major practical challenge when trying to prosecute FGM offenders in local Nigerian courts?

options.A: Mandatory legalization of the practice by state governors
options.B: Complete absence of any federal or state legal frameworks
options.C: Immunity granted to all traditional practitioners by the constitution
options.D: Lack of training and logistical support for police and judiciary

explanation: Correct! Law enforcement officers sometimes struggle to investigate and take these cases to court due to limited resources and specialized training.

question: What is true about getting valid informed consent from a patient?

options.A: It is only necessary if the research involves major surgical procedures
options.B: It transfers the ownership of the patient's medical records to the researcher
options.C: It involves clear communication and genuine voluntary agreement, not just a signature
options.D: It can be waived by the nurse if the patient looks too tired to read

explanation: You got it! Consent isn't just about ticking a box or signing a paper—it's an ongoing conversation where the patient truly understands and freely agrees to take part.

question: Where can polyvalent nurses put their skills to work?

options.A: Solely in out-patient community pharmacies
options.B: Only within government-run research laboratories
options.C: Across various urban and rural health facilities
options.D: Exclusively in private intensive care units

explanation: You nailed it! Because they are so adaptable, polyvalent nurses can fit right into almost any healthcare setting, from city hospitals to village clinics.

question: Why do care staff encourage residents to do parts of their morning routine all by themselves?

options.A: To reduce the total number of staff members needed on duty
options.B: To eliminate the need for any individualized service plans
options.C: To comply with federal acute care hospital regulations
options.D: To prevent physical decline caused by lack of use

explanation: Great thinking! Letting residents do what they can manage preserves their muscle strength, coordination, and sense of pride.

question: Why are open-ended questions preferred during reproductive health counselling?

options.A: They shorten the time needed to complete patient registration
options.B: They encourage clients to share their thoughts and concerns fully
options.C: They ensure the nurse makes all the final medical decisions
options.D: They prevent clients from asking complicated medical questions

explanation: Open-ended questions allow clients to express their true feelings and personal stories rather than giving a simple one-word answer. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T022#GNS226_U6_T022_h4)

question: Why is it important to document what the lesion or discharge looks like after swabbing?

options.A: To provide a clear baseline for tracking clinical progress
options.B: To prove to the laboratory technician that a swab was necessary
options.C: To satisfy insurance requirements for billing the laboratory test
options.D: To ensure the patient remembers how the symptoms appeared

explanation: Writing a clear description gives the healthcare team a baseline so they can easily check if the treatment is working during the next visit.

question: What is the main goal of using the '5 Ps' framework when taking an adolescent's health history?

options.A: To calculate the exact body mass index of the patient
options.B: To determine the nutritional requirements of the teenager
options.C: To gather a thorough and structured sexual health history
options.D: To diagnose mental health disorders like depression

question: Why is the skin considered our body's primary shield?

options.A: It sits right between our internal organs and the outside world.
options.B: It produces all our red blood cells.
options.C: It pumps nutrients directly into underlying muscles.
options.D: It filters waste straight out of our bloodstream.

explanation: Spot on! Because skin covers our entire outside, it acts as our very first line of defense against everyday hazards. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T3#GNS211_U2_T3_h1)

question: A community nurse wants to store the medical history of a husband, wife, and their children together in one file. Which stationery item should be used?

options.A: A family folder
options.B: An immunization register
options.C: A drug inventory log
options.D: A daily tally sheet

question: What is the most common symptom of a pinworm infection?

options.A: Yellow discoloration of the eyes
options.B: Sudden paralysis of the lower limbs
options.C: Blood in the urine (hematuria)
options.D: Intense nighttime perianal itching

question: A new mother complains of a severe headache, blurred vision, and upper tummy pain 3 days after birth. What is your best response as a nurse?

options.A: Discharge her home to rest
options.B: Report these signs immediately as possible postpartum pre-eclampsia
options.C: Tell her to stop breastfeeding until the headache clears
options.D: Reassure her that it is just normal tiredness

question: An unmarried young girl comes to the clinic asking about family planning, and another nurse loudly criticizes her morals. What is the best way for you to handle this?

options.A: Ignore the situation because nurse-to-nurse conflicts are discouraged
options.B: Gently intervene, take over the client's care, and provide confidential, non-judgmental education
options.C: Agree with the colleague so the young girl learns a lesson about societal expectations
options.D: Report the girl to hospital security for seeking family planning services

explanation: You've got this! Patient dignity and privacy come first. Step in warmly, protect your patient from stigma, and make sure she gets safe, supportive, and confidential care.

question: Why do patients with acute viral hepatitis develop jaundice (yellow eyes and skin)?

options.A: The gallbladder ruptures and releases stored bile directly into the abdominal cavity
options.B: Swelling in the liver blocks bile flow, causing bilirubin to back up into the blood

options.D: The kidneys stop filtering waste products due to a sudden drop in blood pressure

explanation: When the liver is swollen, normal bile drainage gets blocked. This backs up yellow bilirubin pigments into the bloodstream, turning the skin and eyes yellow.

question: Which variable always goes on the bottom (horizontal X-axis) of a scatter diagram?

options.A: The average median score
options.B: The dependent outcome
options.C: The independent variable
options.D: The total patient count

explanation: Remember: the independent (or explanatory) variable always sits comfortably on the horizontal X-axis.

question: What is the primary benefit of herd immunity in a community?

options.A: It replaces the need for personal hygiene and clean water
options.B: It completely eliminates all viruses from the global environment
options.C: It protects vulnerable individuals who cannot receive vaccines
options.D: It guarantees that natural infections never occur again

question: As a nurse, why is the subcutaneous layer (hypodermis) often chosen for giving certain injections?

options.C: It lacks nerve endings, making injections completely painless.
options.D: It consists of hard bone that stabilizes the needle.

question: Which patient will benefit most from a nebulizer instead of a standard inhaler?

options.A: An active athlete who needs a quick rescue puff before playing football
options.B: A severely breathless patient who struggles to coordinate breathing with an inhaler
options.C: A healthy adult who prefers taking their daily maintenance medication quickly
options.D: A patient who experiences dry mouth from using anticholinergic inhalers

explanation: Nebulizers turn liquid medicine into a cool mist that the patient can breathe in easily during normal breathing, making them perfect for someone in severe respiratory distress.

question: Why do hospitals enforce strict double-key storage and witness counts for narcotics?

options.A: To prevent drug diversion and control abuse risks
options.B: To make medication administration take longer for nurses
options.C: To test whether the patient actually needs pain relief
options.D: To ensure the pharmaceutical company makes more profit

explanation: Strict counting and witness rules protect controlled substances from theft, misuse, or illegal diversion. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T1#GNS125_U2_T1_h4)

question: What is the main reason for keeping vaccines cold in a cold chain during transport and storage?

options.A: To stop healthcare workers from accidentally losing the vials
options.B: To ensure the biological potency and effectiveness of the vaccine
options.C: To prevent the vaccines from changing into a liquid state
options.D: To make the injection feel cooler and less painful for the baby

explanation: Correct! If vaccines get too warm or freeze, they lose their strength and won't protect the child from disease.

question: What does a public sector nurse typically need to do to qualify for a promotion to a higher grade level?

options.A: Resigning from all professional nursing associations and unions
options.B: Completing the mandatory years on the current rank and passing promotional exams
options.C: Submitting a personal petition directly to the national legislature
options.D: Volunteering to fund hospital equipment purchases out of pocket

explanation: Upward mobility in the civil service requires spending the required time on your current rank and passing your promotional exams.

question: A study shows a link between carrying a cigarette lighter and getting lung cancer. What role does smoking tobacco play here?

options.A: It is a confounding or underlying variable connecting the two
options.B: It is a zero-correlation factor with no medical relevance
options.C: It is an experimental intervention created by the researcher
options.D: It is a statistical error made during data entry

question: What is the name of the first nutrient-rich, antibody-packed milk a mother produces after birth?

options.A: Colostrum
options.B: Surfactant
options.C: Meconium
options.D: Lochia

explanation: Colostrum is liquid gold for the newborn! It is packed with antibodies to protect the baby before the regular milk comes in. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T016#GNS226_U3_T016_h4)

question: Which surfaces in a patient's room need cleaning and disinfecting the most often?

options.A: The outer walls of the hospital storage cupboard
options.B: High ceilings and ceiling fan blades
options.C: High-touch surfaces like bed rails and door handles
options.D: The lower baseboards near the floor corners

question: Why is it important for nurses to know about anti-discrimination policies in healthcare?

options.A: To replace hospital administrators in their daily jobs
options.B: To ensure only male patients receive specialized care
options.C: To guide and support patients who face unfair treatment
options.D: To avoid ever having to speak with patients about gender

explanation: Knowing patients' rights lets you stand up and advocate for them when they face unfair treatment in the clinic. You're well on your way to becoming a fantastic nurse!

question: What is the medical term for painful menstrual cramps caused by trapped blood behind scar tissue?

options.A: Dysmenorrhea
options.B: Amenorrhea
options.C: Menorrhagia
options.D: Polymenorrhea

explanation: You got it! Dysmenorrhea means painful periods—and the pain becomes severe when scar tissue blocks menstrual blood from flowing out normally.

question: What is the very first nursing action if a patient's gastrostomy tube accidentally falls out?

options.A: Pour sterile water directly into the exposed hole to keep it wet
options.B: Try to force a larger replacement tube into the opening immediately
options.C: Leave the open hole uncovered and wait for the doctor to arrive
options.D: Cover the stoma with a sterile dressing and call the provider

explanation: Gastrostomy tracts can begin to close within hours, so protecting the site and notifying the medical team urgently is vital to allow safe replacement. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T4#GNS212_U1_T4_h7)

question: A patient complains that their prescribed diet cuts out all their favorite cultural dishes and feels impossible. What is your best response?

options.A: Tell the patient they have no choice and must strictly obey the prescription
options.B: Work with the patient to find healthy substitutes and modify their favorite cultural meals
options.C: Ignore the complaint since food preferences do not affect health outcomes
options.D: Advise the patient to stop eating entirely until they adjust to the new menu

explanation: That's patient-centered care! Respecting their culture and tweaking their favorite meals makes it much more likely they will stick to the plan.

question: What is the name of the thick muscular middle layer of the heart wall that pumps blood?

options.B: Epicardium
options.C: Pericardium
options.D: Endocardium
